sources.entry: The mythical 10x programmer - Salvatore Sanfilippo *(author of Redis)*

summary.title: The mythical 10x programmer
summary.one_liner: Salvatore Sanfilippo (antirez, author of Redis) argues that a 10x programmer's advantage comes from multiplicative factors such as experience, focus, design sacrifice, simplicity, knowledge and debugging skill.
keywords: low level understanding of the machine
takeaways: The 10x programmer idea is contested; the author argues that productivity factors combine multiplicatively rather than linearly.
Design sacrifice means giving up a small, costly non-fundamental goal (e.g. 5%) to gain most of the benefit (e.g. 90%), as with best-effort ordering in Disque.
Complexity mostly grows from refusing design sacrifices and from accumulated early design errors; small proof-of-concept designs help avoid this.
Focus (limiting interruptions and internal distractions), experience, debugging discipline and knowledge of data structures and probabilistic algorithms all raise output.
Perfectionism can bias designs toward measurable metrics and away from robustness, simplicity and delivery time.
summary.summary: This short essay by Salvatore Sanfilippo (antirez, author of Redis) discusses whether a 10x programmer really exists and what drives large productivity differences. The author argues that skills such as implementation ability, experience, focus, design sacrifice, simplicity, knowledge of algorithms, low-level understanding and debugging interact multiplicatively. He illustrates the points with personal examples, including the Disque message broker and counting unique items in a stream. It is written as a reflective opinion piece rather than a tutorial, and it ends with the idea of "opportunistic programming".
